This Agenda contains a brief general description of each item to be considered. Copies of the Staff reports or
  other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the Agenda are on file in the Office of
  the City Clerk and are available for public inspection. Any person who has a question concerning any of the
  agenda items may call the City Manager at (310) 603-0220, ext. 200.

  Procedures for Addressing the Council

  IN ORDER TO EXPEDITE CITY COUNCIL BUSINESS, WE ASK THAT ALL PERSONS WISHING TO ADDRESS THE
  COUNCIL SUBMIT YOUR COMMENTS IN ADVANCE TO CITYCLERK@LYNWOOD.CA.US OR FILL OUT A FORM
  PROVIDED AT THE PODIUM, AND TO TURN IT IN TO THE CITY CLERK PRIOR TO THE START OF THE
  MEETING. FAILURE TO FILL OUT SUCH A FORM WILL PROHIBIT YOU FROM ADDRESSING THE COUNCIL IN
  THE ABSENCE OF THE UNANIMOUS CONSENT OF THE COUNCIL.

  PUBLIC ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

  NON-AGENDA PUBLIC ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  THIS PORTION PROVIDES AN OPPORTUNITY FOR THE PUBLIC TO ADDRESS THE COUNCIL ON ITEMS
  WITHIN THE JURISDICTION OF THE COUNCIL AND NOT LISTED ON THE AGENDA. IF AN ITEM IS NOT ON THE
  AGENDA, THERE SHOULD BE NO SUBSTANTIAL DISCUSSION OF THE ISSUE BY THE COUNCIL, BUT COUNCIL
  MAY REFER THE MATTER TO STAFF OR SCHEDULE SUBSTANTIVE DISCUSSION FOR A FUTURE MEETING.
  (The Ralph M. Brown Act, Government Code Section 54954.2 (a).)

  CONSENT CALENDAR
  ALL MATTERS LISTED UNDER THE CONSENT CALENDAR WILL BE ACTED UPON BY ONE MOTION
  AFFIRMING THE ACTION RECOMMENDED ON THE AGENDA. THERE WILL BE NO SEPARATE DISCUSSION ON
  THESE ITEMS PRIOR TO VOTING UNLESS MEMBERS OF THE COUNCIL OR STAFF REQUEST SPECIFIC
  ITEMS TO BE REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR FOR SEPARATE ACTION.

  8.  APPROVAL OF THE WARRANT REGISTER
  Comments:
  City of Lynwood warrant register dated April 4, 2023 for FY 2022-2023. (FIN)

  Recommendation:
  Staff respectfully recommends that the City Council of the City of Lynwood approve the warrant
  register dated April 4, 2023 for FY 2022-2023.

  9.  PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES
  Comments:
  Approving previous meeting minutes for the Lynwood City Council (CC)

  March 21, 2023 Regular City Council Closed Session Meeting
  March 21, 2023 Regular City Council Meeting

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the Lynwood City Council approve the following minutes:

  March 21, 2023 Regular City Council Closed Session Meeting
  March 21, 2023 Regular City Council Meeting

  10.  APPROVAL OF NON-PROFIT APPLICATIONS FOR THE SALE OF SAFE AND SANE
  FIREWORKS
  Comments:
  The purpose of this item is to approve the five (5) qualified applications for the sale of Safe and
  Sane Fireworks during July 1 through July 4, 2023. (CC)

  Recommendation:
  Staff respectfully recommends that the City Council review the item and approve the five (5)
  identified fireworks stands.

City Council Regular Meeting - Page 2 of 107
   11.  REJECTION OF ALL BIDS FOR THE CITYWIDE SLURRY SEAL (PHASE 3)
  PROJECT FY 2022-2023.
  Comments:
  Staff has an implemented citywide slurry seal program that is currently on Phase 3 of the four-
  phase program. Staff sent out the Notice Inviting Bids on the City Website (PlanetBids) where the
  city received four bids. The cost of this project exceeded the engineer's estimate and staff
  recommends that the city council reject all bids and re-advertise in FY 2023-2024. (PW)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled: “A RESOLUTION
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD FOR THE REJECTION OF ALL
  BIDS FOR THE CITYWIDE SLURRY SEAL (PHASE 3) PROJECT FY 2022-2023”.

  NEW/OLD BUSINESS
  12.  COMMERCIAL FACADE GRANT PROGRAM UPDATE
  Comments:
  The Lynwood City Council will consider staff's recommendation to increase the Commercial
  Facade Program grant amount between to $20,000- $25,000. The increase would allow staff to
  move forward with the improvements for some of the applicants. (CD)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  Amend the guidelines for the Commercial Façade Program to increase the grant award between to
  $20,000- $25,000.

  13.  APPROVAL OF THE LYNWOOD PARK MEGA PLAYGROUND PROJECT CONCEPT
  AND AUTHORIZATION TO SOLICIT PROPOSALS
  Comments:
  The Mega Playground is one of many improvements the City of Lynwood is seeking to complete
  in order to enhance outdoor experiences for community residents. Staff is seeking approval of the
  "Space" Concept for the Lynwood Park Mega Playground. If approved, Staff will solicit proposals
  from qualified architects/contractors for Design-Built work. (PW)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled: “A RESOLUTION
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD APPROVING THE LYNWOOD
  PARK MEGA PLAYGROUND PROJECT CONCEPT AND AUTHORIZATION TO SOLICIT
  PROPOSALS”

  14.  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 1757 - GRANTING A
  NONEXCLUSIVE FRANCHISE TO TORRANCE PIPELINE COMPANY
  Comments:
  Torrance Pipeline Company LLC is requesting to extend the existing pipeline agreement. (CC)

  Recommendation:
  Conduct second reading, read by title only and adoption of the attached ordinance entitled, "AN
  ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD GRANTING A
  NONEXCLUSIVE FRANCHISE TO TORRANCE PIPELINE COMPANY TO OPERATE
  AND MAINTAIN A PIPELINE SYSTEM FOR THE TRANSPORTATION OF OIL AND GAS
  UNDER CERTAIN PUBLIC WAYS AND PUBLIC PLACES IN THE CITY OF LYNWOOD;

  15.  REVIEW OF BOARD, COMMISSION AND COMMITTEE MEMBERS & ANNUAL
  BOARDS, COMMISSIONS AND COMMITTEES LOCAL APPOINTMENT LIST
  Comments:
  Review of Board and Commission Members (CC)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council review the list of Board and Commission Members.

  adjustments to these Boards and Commissions, as it deems appropriate, in accordance with the
  rules outlined below.

  SUBJECT:  COMMERCIAL FACADE GRANT PROGRAM UPDATE

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  Amend the guidelines for the Commercial Façade Program to increase the grant award between to $20,000- $25,000.

  Background:

  At its regular meeting of April 19, 2022, the Lynwood City Council approved Resolution No. 2022.065 appropriating $830,000 in ARPA funding for
  program implementation of a Commercial Façade Grant utilizing Coronavirus Local Recovery Funds awarded to the City of Lynwood under the
  American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 (ARPA).

  Utilizing the $830,000 appropriated for Economic Development under the City’s adopted ARPA plan, staff proposed a Commercial Facade Grant
  Program to assist business property owners in the hardest hit commercial areas of the City. The goals of the program are:

  Improve visual quality of the building façades
  Enhance or restore buildings to create attraction for new businesses
  Restore economic vitality and investment confidence
  Assist businesses negatively impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic
  Achieve a high standard of design for individual buildings
  Use of high quality materials and workmanship on building façades

  The grant program established the Business Beautification/Façade Improvement Plan to issue grants of up to $12,000 ($10,000 for direct labor and
  $2,000 for soft costs) to approximately 69 businesses and to retain a service provider to assist in program promotion and implementation. The funds
  would support basic repairs, facade improvements and beautification of high-need commercial corridors in the city affected by COVID -19 closures
  and other safety or quality of life impacts. The amount of the initial individual grant was limited in order to provide the greatest flexibility.

  Three specifically designated commercial area corridors were designated a high priority for the city and required community investment to support
  public safety and enhance the general customer experience. Qualifying property/business owners are those located within city limits on Imperial
  Highway, Atlantic Avenue, or Long Beach Boulevard and storefronts must be visual from the street along one of the identified business corridors.

  Upon approval of the program, staff enlisted an outreach consultant, Mayra Berenice En Vivo, that provided canvasing of the designated corridors,
  conducted monthly workshops to explain the program and provide applications and application assistance. They also provided business resources
  such as financial seminars and business-to-business referrals. The outreach consultant conducted monthly workshops from August- January. On July
  25, 2022, the City’s On-Call Consultant, Avant Garde, was brought in to administer the City’s Commercial Façade Program.

  Discussion and Analysis:

  At the regular Council Meeting of March 21, 2022, staff provided an update to the program. Since the last report an additional nine (9) applications
  have been received. Below is a summary of the applications:

  sixty-nine (69) applications have been received.
  fifteen (15) have been closed/deferred for causes such as ineligible locations, business types, or other reasons.
  thirty-four (29) are still in the review process.
  twenty (25) businesses have qualified for approval. Twelve (12) businesses have reached the bidding process for their desired improvement
  requests. The remaining are in the work write up stage.

  To provide the City of Lynwood and its businesses with the beautification and relief the Commercial Façade Program has intended, it is

  improvements for some of the applicants. Remaining projects that exceed the new grant amount would have to be rescoped and sent out for re-bid.

  Background:

  Staff is seeking approval of the “Space” concept for the Lynwood Park Mega Playground and authorization to
  solicit proposals from qualified architects/contractors for design-build work. The Mega Playground is one of many
  improvements the City of Lynwood is seeking to complete in order to enhance outdoor experiences for community
  residents. The playground theme is “Space” as a tribute to the original playground pictured in the proposed RFP
  attachment.

  Discussion and Analysis:

  The Lynwood Park Expansion Project (Project Number #68.132) was approved as part of the 5-Year Capital
  Improvement Project (CIP) plan and will split into three (3) Phases. Mega Playground Project or Phase 1 of the
  Lynwood Park Expansion Project includes a large, destination playground complex which would expand into most
  of the available space in the designated area. The playground will be separated into age-group play areas and will
  utilize “pour in place” surfacing. A short fence will surround the entire area. A sample of playground scope and
  elements are attached as exhibits C & D in the proposed RFP. The project will include expanded walkways; safety
  lighting; seating areas outside of the playground fence, trash cans and water fountains.

  Phase 2 of the Lynwood Park Expansion Project will include a splash pad water feature, space exhibition, picnic
  seating, shade canopy, a flowering tree and other various amenities. Phase 2 will also have a cloud pavilion that
  can be used for events. The project will include expanded walkways; safety lighting, seating areas, trash cans and
  water fountains.
